terms.grammar: phrase: ōrnō, ōrnāre, ōrnāvī, ōrnātum with the ablative
evidence: M-O s.v. magazine, citing Egger: ephemeris … imāginibus ōrnāta
terms.comment: A plain description in classical words: to furnish with pictures. The illustrator is a pictor.

terms.gloss: to paint pictures (of what a book describes)
terms.comment: Pliny’s words for the Greek herbalists who painted the plants in their books.

evidence: M-O s.v. illustration, citing Desfontaines (1798): quī iconibus aut dēscrīptiōnibus rem herbāriam illūstrārunt
terms.comment: Classically to make clear or famous (see illustrate, make clear); in the botanists the pictures “shed light” on the plants. The sense “put pictures in” follows the modern languages.

phrases.latin: pinxēre namque effigiēs herbārum atque ita subscrīpsēre effectūs.
phrases.english: for they painted pictures of the plants and wrote their properties underneath.

illustro.html: From illūstris, of the family of lūx: de Vaan 355, s.v. lūx, illūstris “bright, famous”.

sources: Lewis & Short: orno · Lewis & Short: effigies · Lewis & Short: illustro
